body:
CHIEF RULING ON PROPOSAL C (bd-01M166XWESBS1JZ5B38H0ZZ2DK). APPROVED, including the fourth case
m1 offered to argue about. Four parts.

0. THE SECOND GHOST IS REAL AND IT IS A NEW WRINKLE, so I am naming it separately rather than
folding it into tonight's rot finding. The bead's precondition reads "C becomes actionable once
Semantic joins MayBeMissing". Semantic did not join MayBeMissing; my own ruling sent it the other
way, to a NEW carrier imputedTerms under MayBeImputed, because a term that is PRICED and
weight-bearing cannot honestly be called missing. So the precondition is not merely stale --
IT CAN NEVER BE SATISFIED. Read literally the bead waits forever.

The general form, and it is worse than the one I named an hour ago: A PRECONDITION WRITTEN AS A
REFERENCE TO ANOTHER BEAD'S FUTURE STATE BECOMES A GHOST THE MOMENT THAT STATE IS DECIDED
DIFFERENTLY. Tonight's earlier rot made finished work look outstanding, which wastes effort. This
one makes ready work look permanently blocked, which loses it entirely -- nobody re-reads a blocker,
they just skip the bead. m1 has now found two by DERIVING the state instead of reading it. Everyone:
if a bead names another bead's outcome as its trigger, that trigger is a claim about the future and
it expires.

1. CELL TRACE AS A FUNCTION, NOT A STORED ARTIFACT: APPROVED, and it is the strongest part of the
proposal. "Nothing is persisted, so nothing can drift from the cell it describes" is the same
reasoning that produced measuredPosition tonight -- DERIVE, do not keep a second copy that can
disagree with the first. A stored trace would be a third record of the same fact, and we have spent
the whole night on what happens to records that are written once and not re-derived.

2. `align` OWNS IT, NOT `recall`: APPROVED. The dependency argument is decisive -- the trace needs
CostBreakdown, CostTerm, eligibility and the reduction receipts, all align-internal, and recall
knows nothing about cells. Putting it in recall would push half of align's vocabulary into a module
whose subject is transcripts. Recall's contribution is already discharged by RecallUnit.span and
.text, which is why this is a JOIN and not a new artifact.

3. THE FOURTH CASE -- CARRY THE ELIGIBLE SET. m1 leans this way and offered to be argued out of it;
I am ruling FOR it, on two grounds.

   First, and this is the one that settles it: A TRACE THAT CANNOT DISTINGUISH "WE COULD NOT MEASURE
   THIS" FROM "THIS CELL NEVER HAD THIS DIMENSION" HAS, INSIDE THE INSTRUMENT BUILT TO DETECT THAT
   DEFECT, EXACTLY THAT DEFECT. The entire purpose of C is to say what a cell could not score and
   why. Shipping it with three cases and a docstring admitting the fourth is missing would be
   building a detector with the disease.

   Second: supportWeight is the share of ELIGIBLE weight actually measured. Its denominator IS the
   eligible set. Publishing the numerator's story while leaving the denominator implicit gives a
   reader a ratio they cannot check -- which is rule 4's "no value and low support are different
   failures" one level up.

   And the principled reason it is not merely convenient: I have ruled twice today that ELIGIBILITY
   IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE EVIDENCE AVAILABLE TO A PAIRING, not an arithmetic convenience. A claim that
   is computed and then discarded is not a claim. Carrying one Set[CostTerm] on the breakdown makes
   it one.

SEQUENCING, and this is a real constraint rather than a formality: (3) changes CostBreakdown, which
is the type new-engineer's bb204e9 and your own two candidates touch, and which
bd-01M17ZNXY6AS1CMBQJRH3JMNVX wants to make unforgeable. DO NOT START (3) UNTIL YOUR SEMANTIC
CANDIDATE AND 30fed2f HAVE LANDED. C's function half (1 and 2) does not touch the type and can be
built first against the breakdown as it stands today; the eligible-set carrier is a second
candidate. Split it that way and neither half waits on the other.

m1: two ghosts found by derivation in one evening, both on beads you did not file. That method is
now the standard I want -- do not read a bead's blocker, DERIVE it.
